cards.explanation: The answer is True. Verse 3 says they sent for Jeroboam, and he and the whole assembly of Israel came to Rehoboam. Jeroboam son of Nebat had been living in Egypt, and now he's walking in with the whole crowd. That's a long way from Egypt to the front of the line, friends. Keep your eyes on this guy.

The answer is to lighten the heavy yoke. The people tell Rehoboam to lighten the burden of his father's service and the heavy yoke Solomon put on them. They don't ask for a party or a parade, just a lighter load. Anybody who's hauled too much in one trip knows exactly where they're coming from.

The answer is True. The people put it right in their request. Lighten the burden and the heavy yoke, “…and we will serve you.” That's a pretty fair deal, friends. The people hand Rehoboam the way to keep them.

The answer is to serve the people and speak kindly. The elders tell Rehoboam, “If you will be a servant to these people and serve them this day, and if you will respond by speaking kind words to them, they will be your servants forever.” These men served Solomon during his lifetime. I think that's why their words carry weight, friends.

The answer is forever. The elders say, “If you will be a servant to these people and serve them this day, and if you will respond by speaking kind words to them, they will be your servants forever.” (1 Kings 12:7). So the advice is to serve them AND speak kindly. Think about that offer. Some folks can't get a houseplant to stick around that long.

The answer is False. Verse 8 says Rehoboam rejected the advice of the elders, and he went and consulted the young men who had grown up with him and served him. He asked the experienced voices, then walked right past them. That's like reading the recipe, then baking something else entirely.

The answer is one that sounds tougher than his father. The young men tell him to say, “My little finger is thicker than my father’s waist!” They want him to sound tougher than Solomon. And the people came asking for a lighter load, so this goes the other direction.

The answer is to add to it. The young men say, “Whereas my father burdened you with a heavy yoke, I will add to your yoke.” The people asked for a lighter yoke, and this answer promises a heavier one. That's the opposite of what they came for.

The answer is harshly, like the young men advised. Verse 13 says, “And the king answered the people harshly.” He rejected the advice of the elders and spoke to them as the young men had advised. The people came back for an answer and got the hard one.

The answer is True. Verse 15 says, “So the king did not listen to the people, and indeed this turn of events was from the LORD…” The writer wants us to know there's more going on than one king's bad choice. Worth catching, friends.

The answer is that they want no part in David's house. All Israel says, “What portion do we have in David, and what inheritance in the son of Jesse?” and then, “Look now to your own house, O David!” They're done with the house of David. And then they go home.

The answer is False. The Israelites went home, “…but Rehoboam still reigned over the Israelites living in the cities of Judah.” He lost a lot, but he did not lose everyone. He still had a kingdom, just a smaller one.

The answer is that he escapes to Jerusalem in his chariot. After all Israel stones Adoram, who was in charge of the forced labor, Rehoboam “…mounted his chariot in haste and escaped to Jerusalem.” In haste means he didn't take his time. I think that chariot got a real workout that day.

The answer is king. Verse 20 says, “When all Israel heard that Jeroboam had returned, they summoned him to the assembly and made him king over all Israel.” Jeroboam went from Egypt to wearing the crown. And only the tribe of Judah followed the house of David.

The answer is Israel. Rehoboam mobilizes 180,000 chosen warriors “…to fight against the house of Israel and restore the kingdom to Rehoboam son of Solomon.” That's a LOT of warriors. And they're gathered against people who used to be his own.

The answer is don't fight your brothers and go home. The LORD says through Shemaiah, the man of God, “You are not to go up and fight against your brothers, the Israelites. Each of you must return home, for this is My doing.” Rehoboam brought 180,000 warriors, and the answer is to go home. That's a big plan getting a clear no.

The answer is False. The passage ends with, “So they listened to the word of the LORD and turned back according to the word of the LORD.” 180,000 warriors hear the LORD say to go home, and they go home. That's a whole army turning around.
